title: An open EFT for dark matter searches with matter-wave interferometers
abstract: Matter-wave interferometers (MWIs) are a genuine quantum probe of dark matter (DM), being sensitive to DM-induced phase shifts and loss of contrast. Treating the interferometer as an open quantum system and the dark sector as its environment, we derive an open EFT to study these signatures using the Schwinger-Keldysh formalism. Starting from a microscopic theory, we derive the interferometer's effective action, which we then project onto the many-body worldline sectors relevant for atom interferometers and MWIs employing mesoscopic objects, i.e., composite-particle interferometers (CPIs). This construction clarifies the heavy-probe limit and organizes phase shifts and decoherence as distinct real-time components of the influence action: the retarded kernel controls the causal response of the environment, while the Keldysh kernel controls environmental fluctuations and hence loss of contrast. At leading order, these kernels reduce to: (i) DM bubble diagrams in the case of four-point interactions, and (ii) dressed in-medium mediator propagators in the case of long-range interactions, where the dressing is provided by the DM environment. Within this framework, we study the signatures of elastic spin-independent sub-GeV DM scattering off nucleons and find that: (i) owing to Bose enhancements below the DM wave-particle boundary, ambitious CPIs could probe Higgs-portal DM with mass below 1 eV in an unexplored region of model space; (ii) for DM coupled to nucleons via a light hadrophilic scalar, the DM background can drive the mediator's in-medium mass tachyonic over much of parameter space; outside these regions, CPIs could probe provide powerful probes of light DM.
summary: This paper constructs an open Effective Field Theory to model how Dark Matter interacts with Matter-Wave Interferometers. By using the Schwinger-Keldysh formalism, the authors derive an influence action that cleanly separates the measurable phase shift from the decoherence. This framework predicts that advanced interferometers can probe light DM in unexplored parameter regions.
main_problem: The paper develops a theoretical framework to study how Dark Matter (DM) interactions manifest as measurable signatures in Matter-Wave Interferometers (MWIs). It aims to provide a unified description of DM-induced phase shifts and decoherence.
main_result: The EFT framework successfully separates phase shift (causal response) and decoherence (environmental fluctuations), predicting that ambitious interferometers could probe Higgs-portal DM below 1 eV or reveal tachyonic behavior in mediator masses.
method: The authors utilize the Schwinger-Keldysh formalism to treat the MWI as an open quantum system coupled to the DM environment, deriving an open Effective Field Theory (EFT) via an influence action.
model_or_system: The system involves Matter-Wave Interferometers (MWIs) and Composite-Particle Interferometers (CPIs) acting as quantum probes. The environment is the dark sector, and the interaction is modeled via an open EFT derived from the Schwinger-Keldysh path integral.
key_observables: Phase shift ($	ext{Re } S_{IF}$) and Decoherence ($	ext{Im } S_{IF}$), which are the measurable signatures of DM interaction.
important_parameters: DM mass ($m_\chi$), coupling constants (e.g., Higgs-portal coupling), and the energy scale of the interaction.
main_assumptions: The analysis extends beyond the standard heavy-probe limit and treats the system as an open quantum system coupled to an environment.
figures_summary: Figure 1 summarizes the logical structure of the open EFT construction, detailing the use of the Closed Time-Path (CTP) and the extraction of phase and decoherence from the influence action.
paper_structure: The paper builds the open EFT using the Schwinger-Keldysh formalism, derives the influence action, and then applies this framework to analyze specific DM interaction types (contact vs. long-range) to predict observable signatures in CPIs.
why_interesting: This work is highly relevant as it merges techniques from open quantum systems (SK formalism) with cutting-edge experimental proposals in AMO physics (MWIs) to probe fundamental physics (DM).
